headline: Nvidia stops shipping licensed Hopper AI chips to China
dek: The interim CEO confirmed it on the earnings call, per The Verge.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What happened
body: Nvidia stopped shipping licensed Hopper H200 chips to China, interim CEO Colette Kress said, per The Verge and Olhar Digital.
She did not explain the reason (The Verge).

points.t: The White House allowed shipments in December 2025.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: A new US rule targets indirect chip access through third-country data centers (TechCrunch).
Jefferies estimates a $44 billion to $62 billion hit to data center revenue (TechCrunch).

items.t: About 600,000 H200s sat in Hong Kong (The Verge).
A report says China seeks the chips (CNBC).

caption.hook: Nvidia stopped shipping licensed Hopper H200 chips to China.
body: Per The Verge and Olhar Digital, interim CEO Colette Kress said on the earnings call that guidance no longer includes licensed Hopper products for China and that the company stopped shipping them. She did not explain the reason. The channel had existed since December 2025, when the White House approved an exception to export restrictions.

The move came the same week as a new Commerce Department rule against indirect access through third-country data centers. Jefferies estimates, per TechCrunch, that the rules could cut $44 billion to $62 billion from Nvidia's data center revenue next year.
